pathway.title: Ttm Technologies Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Earnings, not debt reduction, repaired the credit. Carrying debt was USD 917.8 million at FY2023 and USD 916.2 million at FY2025, yet total leverage fell from 4.52x to 2.22x as EBITDA doubled. It was 2.81x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-28, after the 2026 borrowings for the Swiss purchase and for Epiq. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G1; calculation G2

- The September 2026 acquisitions turn a low-leverage credit into a moderate-leverage one whose outcome depends on an unseen asset. Net leverage of 1.31x at 2026-09-28 is 3.20x pro forma for the Epiq closing on 2026-09-30, applied alone and excluding Epiq's EBITDA; Financial foundation illustrates that USD 100.0 million of Epiq EBITDA would give 2.73x. The Ophir Optics purchase of USD 650.0 million, if debt-funded, would add to it. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation G3; calculation G4

- Free cash flow is the weak link and the investment program is accelerating. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 272.9 million left only USD 21.2 million after USD 251.6 million of net capital spending, against USD 5.8 million a year earlier, and FY2025 free cash flow was negative USD 0.7 million. The 2026 capital spending outlook of USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million implies fourth-quarter spending of USD 158.4 million to USD 178.4 million if it is on the same basis as the nine-month figure, about twice the average quarterly pace. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G6; calculation G7

- Earnings now rest on one engine, the Commercial segment. It earned USD 360.5 million of segment operating income in nine months, more than the group's USD 343.8 million of operating income, and 64.8% of segment operating income against 52.8% a year earlier, while aerospace and defense income of USD 195.7 million was absorbed by USD 212.4 million of unallocated corporate costs and amortization. Management links the growth to AI data center build-out. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation G8

- Liquidity and the maturity ladder are strengths, but interest cover looks backward. Liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 is stated before the Epiq payment and the USD 180.0 million revolver repayment, and pro forma liquidity is not established. Nothing large matures until the 2029 notes: USD 504.0 million in 2029 and USD 386.0 million in 2030 are 53.6% of principal. Cash interest cover of 12.72x excludes the new loans, which are floating rate and add USD 11.0 million a year for each 100 bp rise in rates. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G5; calculation G9; calculation G10; calculation G11

- Customer concentration is high and has moved into receivables. The five largest customers were 44% of nine-month net sales, one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales, and two customers held 30% of receivables at quarter end, so one payment delay would show quickly in operating cash flow, which already leans on a USD 376.0 million rise in supplier payables. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy is mixed rather than adverse. There is no sponsor and there has never been a dividend, but TTM repurchased about USD 100.0 million of shares on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 and authorised another USD 100.0 million, which is 6.25% of the USD 1,600.0 million of debt raised in September; Business & governance rates governance risk as medium. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation G13

runs.text: The main strengths are these. First, earnings have more than doubled since FY2023 and drove total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x at FY2025, which gives the debt a much larger earnings base and lowers refinancing risk. Second, liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 and a maturity ladder with only USD 181.0 million due before 2029 give time to digest the acquisitions. Third, the defense franchise is anchored in long-term contracts with USD 463.5 million of remaining performance obligations and a US Navy radar position, which supports a steadier base beside the data center cycle. Fourth, margin gains in both segments show operating leverage working in the issuer's favour while volumes are high. Fifth, there is no sponsor and no dividend, so no external owner draws cash out. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation G1; calculation G2; calculation G5; calculation G11

The main weaknesses are these. First, the Epiq purchase and the pending Ophir Optics purchase raise net leverage to 3.20x pro forma while the target's earnings are unseen, which makes the next two quarters decisive for creditors. Second, free cash flow is thin and capital spending is stepping up, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth rather than cash generation. Third, earnings are concentrated in the Commercial segment and in AI data center demand, which makes cash flow more cyclical than the defense history suggests. Fourth, customer concentration and the reliance on supplier payables expose operating cash flow to a single payment or terms change. Fifth, the new term loans are floating rate and the reported interest cover of 12.72x does not include them. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation G4; calculation G6; calculation G8; calculation G9; calculation G10

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: TTM agreed on 2026-06-17 to buy two European companies, Swiss Technology Group AG (STG) and ILFA GmbH, in separate stock purchase agreements. The STG purchase closed on 2026-09-16 for cash of USD 401.2 million, with a deal-contingent cross-currency swap of USD 381.1 million against CHF 306.2 million to fix the Swiss franc cost, and the Q2 filing describes a planned revolver drawdown to finance it. STG makes rigid, rigid-flex and flex circuit boards and miniaturized microcircuits in Switzerland and Germany for surgical robotics, hearing aid, medical imaging and implantable-device customers and sits in the Commercial segment. Provisional amounts at quarter end were goodwill of USD 202.5 million, definite-lived intangibles of USD 111.0 million and property, plant and equipment of USD 44.4 million; no pro forma figures are shown because the filing calls the deal not material. The documents do not say whether the ILFA purchase closed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-29_ttmi-20260629.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 14

On 2026-09-30, two days after the quarter ended, TTM bought all membership interests in EDS Intermediate Holding, LLC (Epiq) for cash of USD 1,100.0 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. The purchase agreement is dated 2026-08-15 and names EDS TopCo, LP, TTM Technologies North America, LLC and TTM Technologies, Inc. as parties besides Epiq, and a debt commitment letter of the same date from JPMorgan Chase Bank, Barclays Bank PLC and two Bank of America entities was filed alongside it. The filing says the deal is meant to provide critical technologies and innovative capabilities for aerospace and defense customers. It gives no Epiq revenue, earnings, assets, location or seller ownership and no purchase price allocation, because the information had not been received; preliminary accounting is promised in the fourth-quarter 2026 report. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 46

Three financing steps shaped the debt. On 2026-06-01 the 2026 Credit Agreement replaced the term loan with a USD 400.0 million Amended Term Loan Facility (one-month Term SOFR plus 1.75%, due 2030-05-30) and replaced the USD 150.0 million U.S. and USD 150.0 million Asia asset-based facilities with a USD 1,000.0 million revolving facility due May 2031, of which USD 80.0 million was drawn to repay the Asia facility. On 2026-09-24 TTM issued USD 500.0 million of 6.750% senior unsecured notes due 2034-10-01 (7.05% effective rate), guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries and subject to special mandatory redemption had Epiq not closed. On 2026-09-30 the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement added a USD 300.0 million Incremental Term Loan A due 2031-05-30 and a USD 800.0 million Incremental Term Loan B due 2033-09-30, guaranteed and secured on the same basis as the existing loans, and USD 180.0 million of revolver borrowings was repaid after quarter end. Only the revolver carries maintenance covenants: minimum interest coverage of 2.50:1.00 and maximum leverage of 4.50:1.00, rising to 5.00:1.00 for the quarter of a qualifying material acquisition and the next three quarters. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation F8

Further deals and shareholder returns follow. Ophir Optics, the Ophir Optics business of MKS Inc., is to be bought for USD 650.0 million in cash; the agreement was announced on 2026-10-19 and closing is expected in the second quarter of 2027, with funding not stated. Two further European acquisitions, called immaterial and not named, are expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million, citing a plan to invest a further USD 400.0 million in capacity for AI infrastructure. On 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 TTM repurchased about 1,159 thousand shares for about USD 100.0 million, using up the 2025 program, and on 2026-10-27 the board authorised a new program of up to USD 100.0 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20

Not stated in the documents read: pricing of the incremental term loans, any leverage after the 2026-09-30 borrowings, Epiq's earnings and sellers, how Ophir Optics will be funded, and the funding source of the share repurchases. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt, liquidity and leverage from the five supplied filings, to the latest balance sheet at 2026-09-28, with the events after it flagged and kept out of the period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported leverage is moderate but understates what creditors now hold: net debt of USD 767.5 million was 1.31x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-28, before the USD 1,100.0 million Epiq purchase that, on stated amounts, lifts it to 3.20x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C16; calculation C18; calculation C22; calculation C41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings growth, not debt paydown, drove total leverage from 4.52x in FY2023 to 2.22x in FY2025. Free cash flow is thin: capital spending of USD 251.6 million left only USD 21.2 million of the USD 272.9 million operating cash flow of the first nine months of 2026, and that flow leaned on a USD 376.0 million rise in payables.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C17; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carrying debt was essentially unchanged from FY2023 to FY2025, so the fall in total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x came from earnings: EBITDA rose from USD 203.0 million to USD 411.9 million as net sales grew from USD 2,232.6 million to USD 2,906.3 million, and the goodwill impairments of FY2023 and FY2024, which reported EBITDA does not add back, ended. In 2026 the direction reversed: debt rose by USD 727.7 million to USD 1,643.9 million while cash rose by USD 375.1 million, so net debt rose by USD 352.6 million, mainly to pay USD 369.1 million, net of cash acquired, for Swiss Technology Group AG, and net leverage moved from 1.01x to 1.31x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, pages 85–87; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C18; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C43

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover rose from 4.24x in FY2023 to 8.92x in FY2025 and 12.72x on a last-twelve-months basis because EBITDA doubled while cash interest was broadly unchanged. That cover looks backward: scheduled interest of USD 65.0 million falls due within a year on debt at 2026-09-28, before the Incremental Facilities, and the 2034 senior unsecured notes alone cost USD 33.8 million a year, so 12.72x overstates the cover creditors now have.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C19; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was carried by working capital rather than earnings alone. In the first nine months of 2026 receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 574.9 million and payables supplied USD 376.0 million, and all working capital lines together were a net use of USD 169.7 million. Equipment of USD 167.3 million sat unpaid in payables, USD 104.7 million more than a year earlier, so cash capital spending of USD 251.6 million understates what has been committed, and income taxes payable of USD 50.6 million indicate tax expense still to be paid in cash. Free cash flow was USD 21.2 million against USD 5.8 million a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C38; calculation C37; calculation C27; calculation C45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-28 was USD 1,610.2 million, cash of USD 876.3 million plus USD 733.9 million of revolver availability, with USD 241.1 million of the cash in foreign subsidiaries; it is stated before the Epiq payment and the USD 180.0 million revolver repayment that followed. The maturity ladder is light until 2029: USD 181.0 million falls in the rest of 2026, USD 5.0 million in 2027 and USD 3.0 million in 2028, then USD 504.0 million in 2029 and USD 386.0 million in 2030. The Incremental Facilities add USD 300.0 million maturing in 2031 and USD 800.0 million in 2033.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C25; calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C46

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At 2026-09-28 the first-priority secured term loan (USD 399.0 million) and revolver (USD 260.0 million) rank ahead of the 2029 and 2034 senior unsecured notes (USD 500.0 million each). Cumulative principal through the notes is 2.84x last-twelve-months EBITDA against 2.81x on carrying value. Operating and finance leases, supplier finance and customer deposits sit outside the debt lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation C20; calculation C40; calculation C17; calculation C47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contract liabilities were USD 202.3 million against USD 175.6 million at year-end 2025, long-term customer deposits fell from USD 23.5 million to USD 17.6 million after USD 5.8 million was refunded, and supplier finance obligations carried in payables rose from USD 12.5 million to USD 21.5 million. These are small beside payables of USD 1,032.7 million, but they fund working capital and would reverse if customers or banks withdrew.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C39; calculation C48

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, a stricter measure than a lender-defined one: stock-based compensation of USD 61.7 million and acquisition-related and other charges of USD 18.5 million in the first nine months of 2026 are charged against it. Capital spending is gross in the annual reports and net in the interim reports, so a last-twelve-months free cash flow is not calculable, and segment reporting changed twice, so annual segment history does not compare with 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation C35; calculation C49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After 2026-09-28 the Epiq purchase closed on 2026-09-30 for USD 1,100.0 million of cash, funded by the Incremental Facilities and part of the proceeds of the 2034 notes; USD 180.0 million of revolver debt was repaid; shares costing about USD 100.0 million were bought on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27, with a further USD 100.0 million authorized on 2026-10-27; and an agreement to buy Ophir Optics for USD 650.0 million, announced on 2026-10-19, is expected to close in the second quarter of 2027. The 2026 capital expenditure outlook is USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C50

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that the Incremental Facilities of USD 1,100.0 million equal the Epiq price, so on stated amounts the cash and revolver availability of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 was left largely in place, and the 3.20x pro forma net leverage overstates leverage if Epiq earns material EBITDA, which is not supplied. As an illustration only, USD 100.0 million of Epiq EBITDA would put pro forma net leverage at 2.73x. The view would change with Epiq's reported EBITDA and purchase accounting in the fourth quarter 2026 report, an adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, the revolver availability after closing, and the reported covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C25; calculation C22; calculation C34; calculation C51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Epiq's results, balance sheet and purchase price allocation are in no supplied document, so the pro forma figures use stated transaction amounts only and exclude Epiq's own earnings, cash and debt, fees and closing adjustments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's covenant ratios are not printed and the 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous, so scheduled amortization and covenant headroom are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events after the 2026-09-28 balance sheet, each flagged with its date and kept out of the period figures: the Epiq acquisition closed on 2026-09-30; the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement and the Incremental Facilities took effect on 2026-09-30; revolver debt was repaid after the quarter end on a date the filing does not give; shares were repurchased on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27; a new share repurchase authorization was approved on 2026-10-27; and an agreement to acquire Ophir Optics was announced on 2026-10-19 with closing expected in the second quarter of 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carrying values sum to the balance sheet Total Debt of 1,643,872 thousand (497,978 + 490,961 + 394,933 + 260,000). The revolver issuance costs of 5,385 thousand sit in other non-current assets, so its carrying value equals its principal. The Incremental Facilities (Term Loan A of 300,000 thousand maturing 2031-05-30 and Term Loan B of 800,000 thousand maturing 2033-09-30) were funded on 2026-09-30, after the balance sheet date, and are not instruments at the latest balance sheet date. The 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous, so the annual amortization shown is the 4,000 thousand current portion on the balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Segment sales include intersegment sales; the sum of each period equals reported net sales after eliminations. The corporate row is calculated as consolidated operating income less the segment total, which equals the issuer-itemised unallocated amounts (restructuring, impairment, acquisition-related charges, stock-based compensation, other corporate expenses and amortization). The 2026 reports moved RF&S Components into A&D, so the FY2023 to FY2025 rows and the 2026 rows are on different bases and are not comparable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each check shows its inputs. Money amounts are in US$ millions to three decimals, exact from the thousands printed; the ratios are the register values.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Epiq's financial statements, results, balance sheet and purchase price allocation are not in any supplied document, so pro forma leverage cannot include Epiq's earnings, cash or debt; it restricts the post-closing leverage, cover and liquidity figures, severity High, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report or Epiq's own statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is built from operating income plus depreciation and amortization for every period; it restricts comparison with lender-defined leverage and with covenant tests, severity Medium, and the action is an earnings release with a reconciliation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant ratio values and definitions for the revolver tests are not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable for any period; severity Medium, and the action is the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The undrawn committed facilities at the end of FY2023 are not in the supplied annual reports, so the FY2023 liquidity row has cash only; severity Low, and the action is the FY2023 annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Several income statement and cash flow cells are dashes in the source (impairment of goodwill, loss on extinguishment of debt, gain on sale of subsidiary, derivative losses, proceeds of capital-related government incentives and others) and are written as not supplied, not zero; severity Low, and the action is none beyond confirming the dashes mean nil.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Some lines exist in only some reports (for example derivative losses appear only in the 2026 interim statements and purchases of equipment are gross in annual reports and net in interim reports), so those cells are not supplied for the other columns; severity Medium for capital spending, which makes last-twelve-months capital spending and free cash flow not calculable, and the action is a consistent capital spending series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous between a quarterly and an annual 1% of the original principal; it restricts the scheduled amortization shown for the term loan; severity Medium, and the action is the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment reporting changed in 2025 and again in 2026 and no annual series is on the 2026 basis, so segment trend across annual and interim periods is not comparable; severity Medium, and the action is a recast annual segment table.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisition accounting for Swiss Technology Group AG is provisional and the filing presents no pro forma information, so goodwill, intangibles and the post-acquisition earnings contribution may change; severity Low, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No quarterly statement for the fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied, so that quarter is derived as the full year less nine months and labelled calculated; severity Low, and the action is none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Period start dates are not printed and are set to the day after the previous period end; severity Low, and the action is none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The share of cash held by foreign subsidiaries, USD 241.1 million at 2026-09-28, may be subject to repatriation tax if remitted, although the issuer states no material unaccrued tax; severity Low, and the action is none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital spending is not split between maintenance and growth in any filing, so those lines are not supplied; severity Medium, and the action is management disclosure of the split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pending Ophir Optics acquisition is not completed, so no net debt effect or pro forma figure is stated for it and its cells are not supplied; severity Low, and the action is the report after closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The share repurchase is dated as a two-day window and not by purchase, so its date cell is not supplied; severity Low, and the action is none.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and operating-model fact pack for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied filings and the Source readiness analysis; transactions after the 2026-09-28 balance sheet are described only as far as those filings describe them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TTM Technologies is now a larger, more acquisitive and more data-center-dependent credit than its last annual report shows, and creditors rely on an unseen USD 1,100.0 million acquisition, Epiq, closed two days after quarter end and funded entirely from new notes and term loans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trading is strong on the evidence supplied: nine-month net sales rose 43.2% and operating margin reached 11.3%. The documents give no Epiq results, no holder percentages and no leverage after the new borrowings, and three further acquisitions are pending, so the combined effect on creditors is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation F2; calculation F3; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Acquisitions now drive the risk profile more than operations do. Consideration announced or completed since 2026-06-17 totals USD 2,151.2 million: USD 401.2 million for STG (closed 2026-09-16), USD 1,100.0 million for Epiq (closed 2026-09-30) and USD 650.0 million for Ophir Optics (agreed 2026-10-19, closing expected in the second quarter of 2027). New debt of USD 1,600.0 million was raised between 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-30, which concentrates integration, leverage and refinancing risk in one quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation F7; calculation F8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings base has shifted toward AI-driven data center circuit boards, which makes cash flow more cyclical than the defense-heavy history suggests. Data center and networking was 39% of nine-month net sales against 30% a year earlier, while aerospace and defense fell to 37% from 45%; the Commercial segment was 62.3% of net sales against 53.3%. Management attributes the growth to continued build-out of AI data centers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation F4; calculation F6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is high and steady in sales but has risen in receivables. The five largest customers were 44% of nine-month net sales in both years, one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales, and two customers held 30% of receivables at quarter end against one customer at 14% at the prior year-end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified, so the governance risk comes from management's capital allocation rather than sponsor extraction, but that rests on a proxy statement that was not supplied. Management has never paid a dividend, yet it repurchased about USD 100.0 million of shares on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27, about a month after raising USD 1,600.0 million of debt, and authorised a further USD 100.0 million program.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash generation does not yet cover the investment program. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 272.9 million was almost fully absorbed by net capital spending of USD 251.6 million, and the STG purchase took a further USD 369.1 million net of cash acquired; operating cash flow leaned on a USD 376.0 million rise in supplier payables while receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 574.9 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported figures stop before Epiq. The balance sheet date precedes the closing by two days, Epiq's initial accounting and financial information had not been received by the filing date, and the STG accounting is provisional, so every figure above describes TTM without its largest acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is earnings momentum and liquidity. Third-quarter segment operating margin was 18.5% in aerospace and defense and 21.1% in Commercial, against 16.3% and 14.7% a year earlier. Cash was USD 876.3 million, USD 733.9 million of revolver capacity was available, and management states compliance with every covenant at 2026-09-28. Epiq is described as adding critical technologies for defense customers, which, if its earnings are defense-linked and stable, would rebalance the mix toward aerospace and defense. Against that, the 75.3% fixed-rate share of debt predates the floating-rate term loans, and the cash balance appears to include the proceeds of the 2034 notes raised four days before quarter end, which were used after quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows Epiq earnings that comfortably service the USD 1,100.0 million price, if data center demand holds without a rise in customer concentration, and if the pending acquisitions are funded from cash flow rather than new debt. It would worsen if Epiq's earnings are thin or cyclical, if Ophir Optics is debt-funded on top of the September borrowings, or if share repurchases continue while capital spending runs ahead of operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Epiq's financial statements and purchase price allocation were not received by the filing date, so the conclusion on whether the USD 1,100.0 million price is supported by earnings stays a statement about structure and funding, not about value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists reflects what the documents disclose, not a confirmed fact; holder percentages, board independence and related-party dealings are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest filing was signed 21 days before the as-of date, so the conclusion that three acquisitions are pending may be out of date and the status of ILFA, named in June but not in October, is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment structure changed twice and end-market categories were recast, so the mix-shift conclusion compares recast figures and cannot be traced to a single annual series.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration is stated on different bases across filings (five largest, ten largest, one or two customers), so the conclusion that concentration is steady rests on the five-largest series only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TTM agreed on 2026-06-17 to buy two European companies, Swiss Technology Group AG (STG) and ILFA GmbH, in separate stock purchase agreements. The STG purchase closed on 2026-09-16 for cash of USD 401.2 million, with a deal-contingent cross-currency swap of USD 381.1 million against CHF 306.2 million to fix the Swiss franc cost, and the Q2 filing describes a planned revolver drawdown to finance it. STG makes rigid, rigid-flex and flex circuit boards and miniaturized microcircuits in Switzerland and Germany for surgical robotics, hearing aid, medical imaging and implantable-device customers and sits in the Commercial segment. Provisional amounts at quarter end were goodwill of USD 202.5 million, definite-lived intangibles of USD 111.0 million and property, plant and equipment of USD 44.4 million; no pro forma figures are shown because the filing calls the deal not material. The documents do not say whether the ILFA purchase closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-09-30, two days after the quarter ended, TTM bought all membership interests in EDS Intermediate Holding, LLC (Epiq) for cash of USD 1,100.0 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. The purchase agreement is dated 2026-08-15 and names EDS TopCo, LP, TTM Technologies North America, LLC and TTM Technologies, Inc. as parties besides Epiq, and a debt commitment letter of the same date from JPMorgan Chase Bank, Barclays Bank PLC and two Bank of America entities was filed alongside it. The filing says the deal is meant to provide critical technologies and innovative capabilities for aerospace and defense customers. It gives no Epiq revenue, earnings, assets, location or seller ownership and no purchase price allocation, because the information had not been received; preliminary accounting is promised in the fourth-quarter 2026 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three financing steps shaped the debt. On 2026-06-01 the 2026 Credit Agreement replaced the term loan with a USD 400.0 million Amended Term Loan Facility (one-month Term SOFR plus 1.75%, due 2030-05-30) and replaced the USD 150.0 million U.S. and USD 150.0 million Asia asset-based facilities with a USD 1,000.0 million revolving facility due May 2031, of which USD 80.0 million was drawn to repay the Asia facility. On 2026-09-24 TTM issued USD 500.0 million of 6.750% senior unsecured notes due 2034-10-01 (7.05% effective rate), guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries and subject to special mandatory redemption had Epiq not closed. On 2026-09-30 the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement added a USD 300.0 million Incremental Term Loan A due 2031-05-30 and a USD 800.0 million Incremental Term Loan B due 2033-09-30, guaranteed and secured on the same basis as the existing loans, and USD 180.0 million of revolver borrowings was repaid after quarter end. Only the revolver carries maintenance covenants: minimum interest coverage of 2.50:1.00 and maximum leverage of 4.50:1.00, rising to 5.00:1.00 for the quarter of a qualifying material acquisition and the next three quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Further deals and shareholder returns follow. Ophir Optics, the Ophir Optics business of MKS Inc., is to be bought for USD 650.0 million in cash; the agreement was announced on 2026-10-19 and closing is expected in the second quarter of 2027, with funding not stated. Two further European acquisitions, called immaterial and not named, are expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million, citing a plan to invest a further USD 400.0 million in capacity for AI infrastructure. On 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 TTM repurchased about 1,159 thousand shares for about USD 100.0 million, using up the 2025 program, and on 2026-10-27 the board authorised a new program of up to USD 100.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Not stated in the documents read: pricing of the incremental term loans, any leverage after the 2026-09-30 borrowings, Epiq's earnings and sellers, how Ophir Optics will be funded, and the funding source of the share repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance review status: ready with limitations. The five filings are primary and usable; the missing proxy statement and Epiq information limit ownership and acquisition conclusions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Ttm Technologies Inc presents Medium governance risk. The key supported behavior is a rapid, debt-funded acquisition program followed by share repurchases, which matters because new debt and shareholder returns compete for the same cash and implies tighter creditor cushion until Epiq's earnings are shown. Countervailing evidence is strong earnings growth, no dividend history and a large liquidity buffer. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and Epiq's financial statements. Governance review completed with limitations. Governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: Epiq information, proxy statement and executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied filings with the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses; reported figures run to 2026-09-28 and later events are flagged, not blended in.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TTM's fundamental credit is adequate and improving on earnings but now acquisition-dependent: net leverage of 1.31x at 2026-09-28 becomes 3.20x pro forma for the Epiq closing on 2026-09-30, and thin free cash flow leaves little cushion if AI-driven demand slows.

fields.value: Earnings are the support: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 584.3 million is 2.88 times the USD 203.0 million of FY2023, and liquidity was USD 1,610.2 million before the Epiq payment. The 3.20x uses stated transaction amounts and excludes Epiq's own EBITDA, which is not supplied, so leverage after the acquisition is not established.

fields.value: - Earnings, not debt reduction, repaired the credit. Carrying debt was USD 917.8 million at FY2023 and USD 916.2 million at FY2025, yet total leverage fell from 4.52x to 2.22x as EBITDA doubled. It was 2.81x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-28, after the 2026 borrowings for the Swiss purchase and for Epiq.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G1; calculation G2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The September 2026 acquisitions turn a low-leverage credit into a moderate-leverage one whose outcome depends on an unseen asset. Net leverage of 1.31x at 2026-09-28 is 3.20x pro forma for the Epiq closing on 2026-09-30, applied alone and excluding Epiq's EBITDA; Financial foundation illustrates that USD 100.0 million of Epiq EBITDA would give 2.73x. The Ophir Optics purchase of USD 650.0 million, if debt-funded, would add to it.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation G3; calculation G4

fields.value: - Free cash flow is the weak link and the investment program is accelerating. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 272.9 million left only USD 21.2 million after USD 251.6 million of net capital spending, against USD 5.8 million a year earlier, and FY2025 free cash flow was negative USD 0.7 million. The 2026 capital spending outlook of USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million implies fourth-quarter spending of USD 158.4 million to USD 178.4 million if it is on the same basis as the nine-month figure, about twice the average quarterly pace.

fields.value: - Earnings now rest on one engine, the Commercial segment. It earned USD 360.5 million of segment operating income in nine months, more than the group's USD 343.8 million of operating income, and 64.8% of segment operating income against 52.8% a year earlier, while aerospace and defense income of USD 195.7 million was absorbed by USD 212.4 million of unallocated corporate costs and amortization. Management links the growth to AI data center build-out.

Nothing large matures until the 2029 notes: USD 504.0 million in 2029 and USD 386.0 million in 2030 are 53.6% of principal. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against caution is that the earnings base is large and still rising: EBITDA margin reached 15.3% on a last-twelve-months basis, reported net leverage was only 1.31x before Epiq, management states covenant compliance, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations at 2026-09-28. If Epiq earns material EBITDA, the 3.20x overstates leverage, and the Incremental Facilities equal the Epiq price, so the revolver headroom was largely preserved. Epiq is described as adding technology for defense customers, which could rebalance a mix that is now led by data center sales.

fields.value: The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows Epiq EBITDA near or above the illustration, free cash flow turns clearly positive after capital spending, and Ophir Optics is funded without new debt. It would weaken if data center and networking sales fall from their third-quarter level of USD 498.0 million, if capital spending runs at the implied fourth-quarter pace without a matching rise in operating cash flow, or if repurchases continue while leverage is elevated after the acquisitions.

fields.value: - Epiq's EBITDA, cash, debt and fees are not supplied, so the pro forma net leverage of 3.20x is a stated-amounts figure and the conclusion on post-acquisition leverage is a range around it, not a point.

fields.value: - EBITDA is constructed without add-backs and annual capital spending is gross while interim spending is net, so last-twelve-months free cash flow is not calculable and the cash-generation conclusion rests on nine-month and annual figures only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management forecast beyond the capital spending outlook is supplied, so the outlook and downside conclusions are qualitative and carry no stress numbers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are these. First, earnings have more than doubled since FY2023 and drove total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x at FY2025, which gives the debt a much larger earnings base and lowers refinancing risk. Second, liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 and a maturity ladder with only USD 181.0 million due before 2029 give time to digest the acquisitions. Third, the defense franchise is anchored in long-term contracts with USD 463.5 million of remaining performance obligations and a US Navy radar position, which supports a steadier base beside the data center cycle. Fourth, margin gains in both segments show operating leverage working in the issuer's favour while volumes are high. Fifth, there is no sponsor and no dividend, so no external owner draws cash out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation G1; calculation G2; calculation G5; calculation G11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are these. First, the Epiq purchase and the pending Ophir Optics purchase raise net leverage to 3.20x pro forma while the target's earnings are unseen, which makes the next two quarters decisive for creditors. Second, free cash flow is thin and capital spending is stepping up, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth rather than cash generation. Third, earnings are concentrated in the Commercial segment and in AI data center demand, which makes cash flow more cyclical than the defense history suggests. Fourth, customer concentration and the reliance on supplier payables expose operating cash flow to a single payment or terms change. Fifth, the new term loans are floating rate and the reported interest cover of 12.72x does not include them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation G4; calculation G6; calculation G8; calculation G9; calculation G10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TTM Technologies makes printed circuit boards, RF and microwave components and assemblies, and engineered mission systems, and sells to equipment makers, contract manufacturers, distributors and governments. About 59% of nine-month net sales came from operations outside the United States, revenue is mostly recognized over time as customer-specific products are built, and the business is not seasonal. The credit link is that long-term defense contracts and a diversified customer list support cash-flow visibility, while the AI-driven commercial boom, high fixed costs and acquisition debt make debt service more cyclical than the defense history alone would suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: TTM is a widely held public company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in the documents read, so sponsor extraction is not the risk; holder percentages sit in a proxy statement not supplied. The borrower is the parent, the notes and credit facilities are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries only, and 63.1% of long-lived assets and USD 241.1 million of cash sit outside the United States, so the guarantee package covers domestic subsidiaries only and claims on foreign operating assets rank behind those subsidiaries' own creditors, which is structural subordination; foreign subsidiary borrowers may draw up to USD 300.0 million of the revolver. Epiq joined as a guarantor on 2026-09-30. Ranking and collateral are for the Structural priority analysis; this module records that the secured term loan and revolver pledge only 65% of certain foreign subsidiaries' stock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue rests on two engines: defense electronics sold through government budgets and long-term contracts, and commercial circuit boards for AI data centers, automotive and medical customers. Data center and networking was 39% of nine-month net sales against 30%, aerospace and defense 37% against 45%, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations with about 55% to be recognized within 12 months. Pricing power is only partly evidenced: gross margin rose 2.0 percentage points to 22.4% on volume and mix, quick-turn work earns premium pricing, but no contract pass-through of raw material costs is described. Revenue is therefore predictable in defense, cyclical and concentrated in data center and networking, and moderately recurring overall; the implication is that cash flow durability is adequate rather than strong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management states that operating costs are relatively fixed and that small revenue shortfalls reduce operating margin, so operating leverage works both ways: gross margin rose to 22.4% and operating margin to 11.3% on higher volume, and the same fixed base would amplify a slowdown. Unallocated corporate costs are also growing, with stock-based compensation of USD 61.7 million against USD 29.6 million and other corporate costs of USD 103.5 million against USD 66.4 million in nine months, which reduces the margin that segment profit converts into group profit. Raw materials such as copper and gold are exposed to price swings and some components have sole sources. Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure, but not against a sharp fall in data center orders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is heavy and rising: gross purchases of USD 292.6 million in FY2025 were 10.1% of net sales, nine-month net purchases of USD 251.6 million in 2026 were 8.2%, and equipment of USD 167.3 million was unpaid in payables. The filings do not split maintenance from growth spending, so flexibility cannot be measured, although the new Eau Claire, Penang and Syracuse capacity is clearly growth-driven and could be slowed. Operating cash flow converts 58.5% of nine-month EBITDA, and free cash flow after capital spending was USD 21.2 million, so EBITDA does not yet translate into durable free cash flow for deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G6; calculation G16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense: printed circuit boards are fragmented with larger, lower-cost Chinese and Taiwanese competitors, while defense systems compete with BAE Systems, Curtiss-Wright, Leonardo DRS, Mercury Systems and Sanmina; the implication is price pressure in commercial boards and a premium for qualified defense work. New entrants face facility security clearances and customer qualification in defense, while the annual report notes that new competitors may enter commercial boards, which limits pricing power there. Buyer power is high because a few customers and contract manufacturers account for a large share of sales and receivables. Supplier power is moderate: laminates and chemicals are broadly available, but some components for assemblies have limited or sole sources. Substitution risk is not discussed in the documents read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and currency factors are material to this credit. Both the US and Chinese governments have put circuit boards under tariffs, about 59% of nine-month sales come from non-US operations, and costs and cash are exposed to the Chinese yuan, Malaysian ringgit and Swiss franc, with a net investment hedge on the Swiss purchase. Defense sales depend on US budget appropriations and contract terminations, and export rules shape competition. The credit effect is margin and cash volatility that is partly outside management's control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the earnings recovery, liquidity, the defense contract base and operating leverage; weaknesses are thin free cash flow, customer concentration, floating-rate acquisition debt and an unseen Epiq. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Epiq and Ophir Optics earnings that add defense technology and diversify away from data center demand, and capacity additions that convert growth into cash. Threats that could weaken credit quality are an AI capital spending slowdown, tariffs on circuit boards, a payment delay by a top customer and further debt-funded acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile supports a view of adequate credit quality. Supports are the rise in EBITDA, liquidity before the Epiq payment, a light maturity ladder and an audited, controlled reporting base; constraints are leverage that jumps to 3.20x pro forma, free cash flow of only USD 21.2 million, concentration in one segment and floating-rate debt. The trend is improving to 2026-09-28 and reversing at the Epiq closing. Missing datapoints are Epiq's EBITDA, cash and debt, covenant definitions and headroom, post-closing liquidity, peer and rating data, and the split of capital spending.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation G3; calculation G4; calculation G5; calculation G6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are AI data center capacity demand, defense budgets and program bookings, and new capacity at Eau Claire, Penang and Syracuse, which together support growth and margin. The headwinds are integration of STG, Epiq and Ophir Optics, capital spending that exceeds operating cash flow, higher interest on floating-rate loans, tariffs and currency swings. Over three to five years the main questions are whether AI demand proves durable rather than cyclical, whether Epiq earnings cover its price, and whether the 2029 notes and 2030 term loan balance are refinanced at acceptable cost; refinancing confidence rests on earnings, which is why a data center slowdown is the key risk to it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-29_ttmi-20260629.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation G11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a pause in AI data center orders or the loss of volume at one of the largest customers; one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales and the five largest were 44% of nine-month sales. The first operational break is lower volume in the Commercial segment, whose fixed cost base would cut margin quickly, and that segment supplied more profit than the whole group. Financially, EBITDA falls while the pro forma net debt of USD 1,867.5 million stays, so net leverage rises above 3.20x, free cash flow turns negative because committed capital spending continues, and the cash cushion funds the gap. Management levers are slowing growth capital spending, suspending repurchases and not closing Ophir Optics; whether they suffice depends on the maintenance share of spending, which is not stated, and on covenant definitions, which are not supplied. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate downturn because liquidity was large and no large maturity falls before 2029, but leverage-based tests and refinancing access become the binding constraints. The observable trigger is a fall in data center and networking sales below the third-quarter level. Primary downside path: a data center slowdown that cuts Commercial segment profit while acquisition debt and capital spending stay fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G4; calculation G8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, TTM presents an adequate business profile supported by a recovered earnings base, ample pre-acquisition liquidity and a defense contract anchor, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-driven leverage, thin free cash flow and concentration in one segment and a few customers. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because operating cash flow depends on supplier payables and capital spending is rising. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Epiq's earnings, data center demand and market access for the 2029 notes and 2030 term loan. The primary downside path is a data center slowdown against fixed acquisition debt and capital commitments. Further analysis would require Epiq's financials, covenant definitions and compliance certificates, post-closing liquidity and rating or peer data. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: acquisition leverage built on an unseen target while free cash flow is thin.
